title: Hackers Built a Botnet That Doesn’t Just Steal Data, It Burns AI Credits
content_md: A campaign linked to Silver Fox is using fake software download sites to infect Windows computers. The pages copy trusted brands and lead visitors to malicious installers. Microsoft says the activity is consistent with the Silver Fox, or Yinhu, campaign with moderate confidence ; it has not attributed the operation to a nation-state actor. The supplied research describes a different threat, the x47.c botnet sold by WraithTools. It does not connect x47.c to Silver Fox. Microsoft’s Silver Fox report also does not document “smart filtering” that shows researchers different download pages. What it does document is changing installer archives that can make simple file-hash checks less reliable. SilverFox Hides Fake Downloads The attack starts when a user reaches a counterfeit vendor page. Microsoft identified sites posing as download pages for products including Microsoft Edge, Razer, Kaspersky, Calibre, and draw.io. The pages use familiar branding and a clear download button. They primarily targeted Chinese-speaking users and China-based operations of multinational organizations, with affected organizations across several industries. In one observed case, a fake Razer page at pc-razerzone[.]com[.]cn sent a user to gehie246[.]com/712down for a ZIP archive named app_setup.6653004.zip .
